newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai firm explains Philippine Camp John loss.
newsitem.headline: Thai firm explains Philippine Camp John loss.

text.p: Land and Houses Plc said on Wednesday its Thai-Philippine joint venture failed to meet a deadline for signing a Philippine development lease agreement because it was not given part of the project's contracted land.

Land and Houses' vice president Adisorn Thananannaraphul said Manuela Land & Houses (ML&H) could not sign the agreement to convert Camp John Hay as the Philippine government's Bases Conversion Development Authority (Basecon) did not deliver all the land earmarked for the recreational resort project.
ML&H bid 1.588 billion pesos to develop and operate the camp, a former U.S. military base in the northern Philippine hill resort of Baguio. Its bid was about four times higher than the next offer.
Adisorn told Reuters he had expected Basecon's decision to declare the Thai-Philippine consortium in default but said the group would seek a refund of its 100 million peso deposit.
He said according to ML&H, the land that Basecon failed to deliver was classified as part of a national reserve that could not be commercially exploited. He did not elaborate.
Adisorn said development of the planned resort at the camp required a $20 million annual investment over at least an initial five years of the 25-year lease.
Land and Houses closed down four baht to 248 on Wednesday.
